```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(MixSIARPFN)
ok <- MixSIARPFN:::networks_ready()   # the code needs the networks (see pfn_networks())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = ok,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, out.width = "100%")
num <- function(x, digits = 2) if (ok) format(round(x, digits), nsmall = digits) else "?"
```

This follows MixSIAR's alligator example script (`mixsiar_script_alligator.R`), based
on Nifong et al. (2015, *Journal of Animal Ecology*, doi:10.1111/1365-2656.12306): American alligators,
two tracers (δ¹³C and δ¹⁵N) and two sources, marine and
freshwater prey. MixSIAR's script fits **eight** models, to ask which of habitat, sex,
size class and body length explain how much each alligator relies on marine prey.
With MixSIAR each model is a separate MCMC run; with MixSIARPFN all eight take a few
seconds, which is what this example shows.

## The data and the eight models

```{r models, eval = TRUE}
models <- list(
  "1: null"                   = list(factors = NULL, cont = NULL),
  "2: habitat"                = list(factors = "habitat", cont = NULL),
  "3: sex"                    = list(factors = "sex", cont = NULL),
  "4: size class"             = list(factors = "sclass", cont = NULL),
  "5: length"                 = list(factors = NULL, cont = "Length"),
  "6: sex + size class"       = list(factors = c("sex", "sclass"), cont = NULL),
  "7: sex + length"           = list(factors = "sex", cont = "Length"),
  "8: sex x size class"       = list(factors = "sex_sclass", cont = NULL))
x <- system.file("extdata", package = "MixSIARPFN")
load_model <- function(m) {
  nf <- length(m$factors)
  mix <- load_mix_data(file.path(x, "alligator_consumer.csv"), iso_names = c("d13C", "d15N"),
                       factors = m$factors, fac_random = rep(FALSE, nf),
                       fac_nested = rep(FALSE, nf), cont_effects = m$cont)
  source <- load_source_data(file.path(x, "alligator_sources_simplemean.csv"),
                             source_factors = NULL, conc_dep = FALSE, data_type = "means", mix)
  discr <- load_discr_data(file.path(x, "alligator_TEF.csv"), mix)
  list(mix = mix, source = source, discr = discr)
}
data <- lapply(models, load_model)
```

There are `r data[[1]]$mix$N` alligators. All models use Residual * Process error and
MixSIAR's uninformative prior, as in MixSIAR's script; the effects are fixed.

```{r isospace, eval = TRUE, fig.height = 5}
plot_data(mix = data[[1]]$mix, source = data[[1]]$source, discr = data[[1]]$discr)
```

## Fitting all eight models

```{r fit}
time <- system.time(
  fits <- lapply(data, function(d) run_pfn(d$mix, d$source, d$discr, alpha.prior = 1,
                                           resid_err = TRUE, process_err = TRUE))
)
```

All eight models took `r num(time[["elapsed"]], 1)` seconds together (the first
includes starting Python and loading the network).

MixSIAR's script compares the models by leave-one-out cross-validation (LOO), which
needs the likelihood at each posterior draw. MixSIARPFN gives marginal posteriors
only, so it cannot compute LOO; what it makes quick is looking at every model's
posteriors.

## How each model compares with MixSIAR

```{r compare-all}
refs <- lapply(seq_along(models), function(i) mixsiar_reference(paste0("alligator_", i)))
rows <- lapply(seq_along(models), function(i) {
  cmp <- compare_mixsiar(fits[[i]], refs[[i]]$draws, refs[[i]]$summary)
  diet <- cmp[!is.na(cmp$w1), ]
  data.frame(model = names(models)[i], diets = nrow(diet),
             mean_gap = mean(abs(diet$pfn_mean - diet$mixsiar_mean)),
             w1 = mean(diet$w1), sd_ratio = median(diet$sd_ratio),
             pfn_seconds = fits[[i]]$seconds, mixsiar_minutes = refs[[i]]$info$minutes,
             psrf = refs[[i]]$info$max_psrf)
})
tab <- do.call(rbind, rows)
knitr::kable(tab, digits = c(0, 0, 3, 3, 2, 2, 0, 3), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Model", "Diet proportions compared", "Mean difference in means",
                           "Mean W1", "Median SD ratio", "MixSIARPFN seconds",
                           "MixSIAR minutes", "MixSIAR largest PSRF"))
```

Each row compares MixSIARPFN's diet posteriors with MixSIAR's for one model (MixSIAR's
"long" run, three chains). For models with a continuous effect, the diets compared are
the global diet at the average length; the curves along length are compared below.
In total, MixSIAR took `r num(sum(tab$mixsiar_minutes), 0)` minutes of computing for the
eight models; MixSIARPFN took `r num(sum(tab$pfn_seconds), 1)` seconds.

## A closer look

The model with the interaction of sex and size class (model 8):

```{r m8, fig.height = 5}
plot_compare(fits[[8]], refs[[8]]$draws, block = "sex_sclass")
```

Diet along body length (model 5), each alligator's posterior from both methods:

```{r m5, fig.height = 3.5}
plot_compare_covariate(fits[[5]], refs[[5]]$pind)
```

And along length separately for each sex (model 7):

```{r m7, fig.height = 5}
plot_compare_covariate(fits[[7]], refs[[7]]$pind, by = "sex")
```

```{r numbers, include = FALSE}
cov_gap <- function(fit, pind) {
  pf <- merge(fit$consumers[, c("consumer", "level")],
              fit$summary[fit$summary$block == "consumer", c("level", "source", "mean")], by = "level")
  pc <- merge(pf, pind[, c("consumer", "source", "mean")], by = c("consumer", "source"))
  mean(abs(pc$mean.x - pc$mean.y))
}
g5 <- cov_gap(fits[[5]], refs[[5]]$pind)
g7 <- cov_gap(fits[[7]], refs[[7]]$pind)
```

**What this shows.** Across all eight models, MixSIARPFN's posterior means differ from
MixSIAR's by `r num(mean(tab$mean_gap), 3)` on average, and along body length each
alligator's posterior mean diet differs by `r num(g5, 3)` (model 5) and
`r num(g7, 3)` (model 7).
